data.name: Mukund
data.gender_notes: Mukund is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mukund is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘muk’, which means freedom or liberation from suffering. The suffix ‘und’ means god or deity. Mukund is also known as the god of wealth and prosperity in Hinduism. The name Mukund carries the meaning “Liberator, God of Wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mukund usually hope their child will grow to embody liberator, god of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the pursuit of spiritual enlightenment and material wealth.
data.etymology: Mukund belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Liberator, God of Wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mukund total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_sanskrit.meaning: God of Wealth, Giver of Boons
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: मुक् (muk) - to release from, to free + कु (kun) - to do + द (da) - to give. In Hindu mythology, Mukunda is a name of Vishnu, who is the giver of boons and the god of wealth. He is also considered as the one who releases one from the cycle of birth and death.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mukund holds significant cultural relevance in Hinduism, representing the deity and god of wealth and prosperity, particularly in North India. It is believed that invoking the name of Mukund can bring abundance, prosperity, and financial success. In some Hindu households, especially in North India, the first born son is named Mukund or a similar name, hoping for his prosperous future.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Mukund signifies the liberation from sufferings and the attainment of ultimate peace and moksha (Salvation or Enlightenment). It is a reminder that material wealth or prosperity is not the ultimate goal in life but a means to facilitate our spiritual journey towards self-realization and enlightenment. Life's ultimate purpose is to seek the blessings of gods and gain emancipation from the cycle of birth and death.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mukund: One who is free from all worldly sorrows and attains supreme bliss through the grace of Vishnu, the preserver god. Symbolizes inner peace and ultimate liberation.

vedic_reference.note: Mukunda is a name of Vishnu in Hindu mythology, who is considered as the giver of boons and the god of wealth. He is also believed to release one from the cycle of birth and death.

historical_references.reference: Mukundadev, a king of the Parmar dynasty who ruled over Malwa in central India during the 11th century. He was known for his devotion to Vishnu and is often referred to as 'Mukundasah'.

Mukunda Ravivarma, a 16th-century king of the Vijayanagara Empire in southern India. He is known for his military campaigns, particularly his victory over the invading army of the Deccan Sultanate in the Battle of Talikota (1565).
